messages:
maria (eng-platform): Quick sync — we've had a handful of customers report confusing client UX because status codes and error payloads vary a lot between endpoints. Sometimes a quota hit shows up as a 500, sometimes as 429, frontend teams can't reliably show a helpful call-to-action. I'm proposing a small, opinionated error contract we can adopt across the API and surface in Console. Basic idea: 4xx = client input, 403 = auth/permission, 429 = throttling/quota, 422 = validation where helpful, 5xx = infra/fallback. Also include a few standard fields in the JSON body (code, message, human_message, can_retry, retry_after). Thoughts? :thinking:

raj (api): +1 to having a single contract. routing layer currently normalizes errors and sometimes collapses them into 500 for legacy reasons (especially when proxying to dedicated/private). We should add a mapping table in router that converts internal error codes to the contract. can_retry is useful but we need to be careful about policy-level retries vs client retries.

sylvia (product): Love standard fields. From a Console/UX perspective we should map to high-level categories (Quota / Auth / Validation / Transient / Internal) and show a short CTA: e.g. 'Request quota increase' or 'Check API key' rather than raw status + code. We should also plan messaging copy for canary rollouts — don't expose internal error codes in the early rollout.

ted (eng-runtime): We have a bunch of internal errors like MODEL_NOT_LOADED, CACHE_STALE, KERNEL_OOM. I agree we should not leak low-level codes to clients. Suggest model: map those to 502/503 with error_category = "infrastructure" in telemetry, and send a stable client_code like "service_unavailable". Keep an internal_details field (for logs/trace only) that is not returned to public clients.

raj (api): Implementation note: router mapping table will look like: 
```
internal -> client
MODEL_NOT_LOADED -> 503 (service_unavailable)
QUOTA_EXCEEDED -> 429 (quota_exceeded)
INVALID_PROMPT -> 422 (invalid_input)
AUTH_MISSING -> 401/403 (auth_error)
```
We can make that table extensible and authoritative in api-proto.

maria (eng-platform): Example payload I'm thinking of (public): 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "code": "quota_exceeded",
  "message": "Request rate exceeded for organization",
  "human_message": "You’ve hit your request quota. See usage or request an increase.",
  "can_retry": false,
  "retry_after": 3600
}
```
Internal telemetry should include original_internal_code, route, model_id, and request_id.

analytics-bot: telemetry suggestion: add tags -> ["error_category","exposed_client_code","router_strategy","model_shard","quota_bucket"]. That will let us build dashboards that separate UI-visible errors from internal infra noise.

sylvia (product): For rollout UX: we should first apply the contract to a small subset of routes (embeddings + simple text gen) and only show the new human_message copy in Console for opt-in orgs. After 2 weeks, flip default and provide fallback copy for older SDKs. Also provide a console-level hover that maps client_code -> friendly text.

ted (eng-runtime): Note on retries: runtime sometimes returns can_retry=true but backend won't support repeated requests (stateful streams). We need to add a field "retry_scope" = ["global","route-only","none"] to avoid erroneous retries causing double-billing.

raj (api): Action items I can run: 1) draft canonical mapping table in api-proto, 2) add router mapping patch (canary), 3) add lint rule to CI to prevent endpoints from returning unexpected status codes.

maria (eng-platform): I'll draft the spec doc + Console copy samples. Proposed rollout: create spec -> run router canary for 10% traffic to us-west -> enable telemetry tags -> product opt-in for Console messages -> full flip after 2 weeks if metrics OK. Can everyone 👍 if they prefer that flow? :thumbsup:

sylvia (product): 👍

ted (eng-runtime): 👍 (but need a follow-up on retry_scope semantics)

raj (api): 👍 — will attach proto PR when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy started for router-mapping-canary on us-west (canary=10%) — id: deploy-2026-03-12-17.

maria (eng-platform): Great. I'll post the spec link shortly and include example Console copy, telemetry dashboard queries, and SDK migration notes. Thanks all.
